San Antonio is a city in the U.S. state of Texas.
The official name of San Antonio is "City of San Antonio".
San Antonio is the most populous city in Greater San Antonio.
San Antonio is the third-largest metropolitan area in Texas and the 24th-largest in the United States as per the 2020 US census.
San Antonio is the seventh-most populous city in the United States.
San Antonio is the second-largest city in the Southern United States.
San Antonio is the second-most populous city after Houston in Texas.
San Antonio was founded as a Spanish mission and colonial outpost in 1718.
The area of San Antonio is approximately 465.4 square miles (1,205.4 km²).
The land area of San Antonio is 460.93 square miles (1,193.8 km²).
The water area of San Antonio is 4.5 square miles (11.7 km²).
San Antonio sits on the Balcones Escarpment.
The altitude of San Antonio is approximately 662 feet (202 m) above sea level.
The primary source of drinking water for San Antonio is the Edwards Aquifer.
Victor Braunig Lake and Calaveras Lake were among the first reservoirs in the United States built to use recycled treated wastewater for power plant cooling.

The racial makeup of San Antonio is 88.4% White, 6.6% Black and African American, 0.2% American Indian and Alaska Native, 2.8% Asian, 0.1% Native Hawaiian and other Pacific Islander, 0.2% some other race, and 1.7% two or more races.
Ethnically, 64.5% of San Antonio's population is Hispanic or Latin American of any race.
San Antonio has a diversified economy with a gross domestic product (GDP) of approximately $121 billion in 2018.
The city of San Antonio and its metropolis were rated the poorest in 2019.
San Antonio has a council-manager system of government.
The city is divided into 10 council districts designed to be of equal population.
Each district elects one person to the city council, with the mayor elected on a citywide basis.

All members of the San Antonio City Council, including the mayor, are elected to two-year terms and are limited to four terms (except for those who were in office in November 2008 and are limited to a total of two terms).

Nirenberg was narrowly reelected in 2019 against conservative challenger Greg Brockhouse.

The San Antonio Fire Department (SAFD) provides the city with fire protection and EMS service.
